title.narrative: UNICEF Children and youth as agents of change for climate resilience
UNICEF Children and youth as agents of change for climate resilience

description.narrative:
The UNICEF country office approached the Embassy of Sweden with a project proposal for 'Empowering children and young people in North Macedonia to be agents of change in reducing community vulnerability to climate change', with a total cost of 15 631 579 SEK for a duration of 36 months during 2020-2023.
The proposed concept is set to: 1.establish foundations for a relevant and consistent platform for knowledge on environmental and climate change issues. It will support the establishment of comprehensive and cohesive learning standards, training of educational and expert staff and provide expert support in this process specifically in the area of environmental education. 2. enable environmentally focused learning, skills building and empowerment for children and youth across all age groups and throughout their education process, both formal and non-formal: • pre-school children learn the foundations of natural sciences and environmental awareness, along with their parents and teachers, to create a basis for action and change; • primary school aged children, acquiring skills to translate learning and awareness into action, and • adolescents and youth, building on and focusing their great capacity to innovate and create their own opportunities and make change in the world around them.

UNICEFs projektförslag har fokus på att ge barn och ungdomar i Nordmakedonien möjlighet att bidra som förändringsagenter för att minska samhällets sårbarhet för klimatförändringar. Projektet, vilket planeras pågå under 36 månader mellan åren 2020-2023, har en total kostnad på 15 631 579 SEK.
Det föreslagna projektet syftar till att:
1. Etablera en bas för en relevant och konsekvent plattform för kunskap om miljö- och klimatförändringar. Projektet kommer att stödja inrättandet av omfattande och sammanhängande inlärningsstandarder, utbildning av utbildningspersonal och expertpersonal samt att ge expertstöd i denna process, särskilt inom miljöutbildning.
2. Möjliggöra miljöinriktat lärande, kompetensbyggnad och bemyndigande för barn och ungdomar i alla åldersgrupper och under hela deras utbildningsprocess, både i formella och icke-formella lärandemiljöer:
• förskolebarn lär sig grunden för naturvetenskap och miljömedvetenhet, tillsammans med sina föräldrar och lärare, för att skapa en bas för handling och förändring; • barn i grundskolan får färdigheter för att översätta lärande och medvetenhet till konkreta handlingar; • ungdomar och unga vuxna utvecklar och fokuserar sina förmågor till att innovera och skapa möjligheter och förändringar i världen.

The overall vision of the project is: A comprehensive and purposeful environmental education is in place, ensuring that teachers: a) are provided with the resources and capacities to deliver engaging content and activities to students; and b) are supported by mechanisms for professional development and peer learning. Students have a wide variety of platforms and tools for experiential, hands-on learning in the natural sciences, but also have access to venues, programmes and opportunities to practice and foster agency, social innovation and entrepreneurship. Ultimately this system creates public demand for solutions to the environmental and climate change challenges and supports young people to actively engage in responding to the increasing risks. There are two specific objectives: Outcome 1. Foundations for relevant and consistent environmental education are established Strengthening the system and services offered to students, parents and teachers to nurture knowledge and skills for problem solving and environmental sustainability. Outcome 2. Children, young boys and girls, are better equipped to actively contribute to and enhance their community’s response to environmental impact and climate change. Empowering children and youth to acquire knowledge, develop skills and actively seek out opportunities and solutions for combating environmental impact and climate change. In doing so, young people will also develop transferable skills to innovate, adapt and overcome challenges in their environment as well as in their own professional development. By providing the four critical aspects of agency - voice, space, audience and influence, children will be empowered to follow through on issues pertinent to their future in a responsible, informed and systemic manner. UNICEF Office in North Macedonia intends to use formal and non-formal learning to empower children and youth to be agents of change. UNICEF through the project activities intends to increase public participation by ensuring that the voice of young people is heard and taken into consideration by developing skills for critical thinking about living in a healthy environment, sustainable development and awareness on climate change and making responsible choices in everyday life.

Decision on Contribution UNICEF support to Empowering Children and Young people in North Macedonia to be agents of change in reducing Community vulnerability to climate change i North Macedonia 14214

description.narrative:
The programme successfully achieved its core intended results by embedding climate and environmental education structurally into the education system. Climate change content was integrated into national curricula (primary and preschool, with spillover into secondary reform discussions), supported by officially endorsed teaching guides, experiential learning materials, and educator training at scale. This moved climate education from ad-hoc or extracurricular activity into the formal education architecture, which was a central intended outcome.
Another major expected result was capacity strengthening of educators and institutions. Approximately 6,000 teachers, preschool educators, advisors, and inspectors improved their ability to deliver experiential, practice-oriented climate education through in-person training-of-trainers, through professional learning communities and online seminars.
A key structural outcome was the establishment of the Experiential Learning Network (ELN) - a coordinated network of scientific institutions, museums, parks, and CSOs that provides curriculum-aligned, hands-on learning opportunities outside the classroom. The ELN institutionalised access to real-world learning environments and linked schools to existing national knowledge infrastructure, shifting experiential climate education from episodic visits to a systematised delivery model. Together with digital tools (e.g. virtual laboratories), this created durable mechanisms rather than one-off capacity-building interventions, directly supporting effectiveness and partial sustainability.
An additional expected result was meaningful youth engagement and agency. Through UPSHIFT and innovation programmes, young people developed concrete, community-level solutions related to climate and environmental challenges. These initiatives translated abstract climate knowledge into applied problem-solving, aligning with the programmes objective of positioning children and youth as agents of change. Though the institutionalization of the UPSHIFT programme was the least advanced by the end of the project phase, institutional recognition of the potential of this approach grew, and resulted in a drive to integrate it into the formal secondary school curriculum by autumn 2026.
An important unexpected result was the depth of institutional ownership that emerged. Government counterparts (notably education authorities) went beyond initial commitments, using programme outputs as direct inputs into ongoing and upcoming education reforms and explicitly requesting continued UNICEF engagement. This exceeded the original scope of support and strengthened the programmes policy leverage.
Finally, youth innovation components generated spillover effects beyond the programme design: heightened demand for participation, continued pursuit of funding by youth teams after programme completion, and visibility at national level. These outcomes indicated stronger-than-anticipated motivation and agency among participants, but also highlighted sustainability risks once external funding ends.
Sida assesses that the results achieved are very satisfactory in relation to the interventions objectives, scope, and level of funding.
The programme delivered outcomes that were highly relevant to its stated purpose - strengthening climate and environmental education and positioning children and youth as agents of change, and did so at a systemic level rather than through isolated activities. Despite significant external disruptions (COVID-19 and political turnover), the cooperation partner adapted implementation pragmatically without diluting strategic intent.
In the following areas results exceeded expectations: curriculum integration, institutional uptake, and youth engagement, which justifies a positive overall assessment even where original delivery modalities or timelines were adjusted.
The main reasons for achievement were a well-grounded intervention logic, strong alignment with national reform processes, and UNICEFs capacity to operate simultaneously at policy, institutional, and practice levels. The partner demonstrated flexibility in response to contextual shocks and made effective use of partnerships to compensate for institutional weaknesses. Importantly, several unexpected results proved highly valuable, including deeper-than-anticipated government ownership and the emergence of civil society actors as functional connectors within fragmented governance structures. These outcomes were not explicit targets but substantially advanced the programmes purpose and long-term relevance.
No indicator available - only a description of the activity results is published
